To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the digital computer-based apnea monitor described herein has been used to monitor infants for apnea during sleep.

(1) a digital computer-based CO2 apnoea monitor has been designed for application in the in-hospital care of near-miss for s.i.d.S. infants; (2) the monitor is based on the detection of the periodicity of the expired CO2 waveform by using Walsh transformations; and (3) the monitor has been successfully applied in the clinical setting for the detection of apnoeic and periodic breathing episodes in near-miss infants during sleep.
the application of Walsh transformation to the CO2 signal is an efficient method for the detection of apnoeic events in infants.

the development of computer methods for the detection of respiratory disorders in infants.
the development of a digital computer-based monitor for apnoea detection and processing in infants.
the development of a digital computer-based system for the automatic on-line detection of apnoea in sleeping infants.

the digital apnoea monitor is a valuable tool for the detection of apnoeic events during in-hospital care of infants.
the Walsh apnoea detection method is a useful tool for the detection of apnoea episodes in infants.
the digital computer method described in this paper is capable of detecting apnoeas in infants with a high degree of accuracy.
